found_values.value: High side on both paths, onboard and external. The ESC pack's return reaches the one star ground point by its own lead, because an ESC's signal has no reference unless the returns meet; a shunt in the return would share current with that ground path. The pack switches are high-side (R3 row: the external module 'is a high-side switch'; V54's question). The sense leads therefore sit at up to 67.2 V to ground. Applied as 'common mode' of the External shunt sense input, and as the common-mode span (5 to 67.2 V) in the Motor monitor's accuracy budget

VBUS is a separate INA238 pin of 0.8 to 1.2 MOhm: 56 to 84 uA at 67.2 V. It is tapped ahead of the IN+ filter resistor so that current does not flow through the resistor and add a shunt-voltage error. Applied as 'bus-voltage connection' of the External shunt sense input
